title: Force, Mass and Acceleration in One Dimension
learningObjectives: Describe how acceleration in one dimension is determined by net force divided by mass for motion with constant mass.
Predict the size and direction of acceleration from the size and sign of the net force.
Explain why zero net force results in constant velocity and no acceleration.

explanations.text: For motion with constant mass in one dimension, acceleration equals net force divided by mass. Larger force produces larger acceleration and larger mass produces smaller acceleration for the same force.

evidence.quote: The acceleration of an object depends on the mass of the object and the amount of force applied.

explanations.text: Acceleration is defined by how velocity changes over time, which connects the force and mass to the resulting change in motion.

evidence.quote: The change in velocity divided by the change in time is the definition of the acceleration a.

explanations.text: The simple relation between force, mass and acceleration assumes constant mass, and when net force is zero the object keeps a constant velocity rather than accelerating.

evidence.quote: Remember that this relation is only good for objects that have a constant mass.
If there is no net force acting on the object, then the object will maintain a constant velocity.

predictions.prompt: Predict the acceleration for the given mass and net force.
Predict the acceleration when the net force acts in the negative direction.
Predict the acceleration for a larger mass with positive force.
